timezone.note: The client converts the selected local day in app-config to the UTC half-open interval [from,to). All synthetic events fall inside 2031-05-10 UTC.

notes: LT-03.5b finite canonical audit journal oracle. It connects the actual dictionary timeline, the actual LT-03.4a accepted batches and their 260 per-file outcomes, the LT-03.4b operational/session descriptors and the LT-03.5a manual return without duplicating their values. Attempt events are expanded from the frozen outcome rows by a declarative state->event recipe (the literal range recipe) and every attempt/phase is unique. All 14 OAS AuditAction values are represented with their exact category and actor/null scope. actor=null is modelled only for an uninitiated LOGIN_FAILED; a blocked author stays in the actor filter list with the historical display-name snapshot and no blocking metadata is invented as an Actor DTO field. Query scenarios declare the literal expected ordered event ids; the module re-derives them from the declared events, filters and cursor bounds. This is an expectation, never measured audit evidence, and no journal/filter/cursor/actor-directory/HTTP transport is implemented.

actors.note: The account is blocked, but it authored an accessible DRAFT_SAVED event, so it stays in /audit/actors. The event carries the display-name snapshot at action time; the actor page carries the current display name. The Actor DTO has no blocking field.

The two-actor claim overlap concurrency scenario of LT-03.4b.
The manual new-key retry scenario of LT-03.4b.

queries.reason: The Moscow day converted to UTC, company filter only, first page in occurred_at DESC then event_id DESC order.
First page of the whole shared journal as it stood before the late login event; the frozen upper bound is the newest event observed at cursor creation.
The second page is pinned to the frozen upper bound; the newer login event must not appear and must not shift the page.
Action filter BATCH_ACCEPTED: exactly one acceptance per primary accepted batch.
The manual return is the only QUARANTINE_RETURNED event; its operation_id equals return_operation_id.
Result filter ISSUE bounded to five events: the ambiguous return recovery and the technical terminal outcomes.
Author filter by the actor user_id (not the display name), bounded to ten events.
Company filter for Nova returns only the Nova dictionary event.
The same filter replayed returns the identical page.
Text filter matches the logical display path of the quarantined attempt and the manual return; the raw search text is never stored on an event.
A window with no events returns items=[], next_cursor=null and newest_event_id=null.
The isolated two-actor overlap universe is queried separately and never merged into the primary day.
The isolated manual-retry universe is queried separately.
The isolated hetero/conflict/sorted accepted selections are a separate alternate history.
The same day and filters are visible differently by role: a WORKER only sees the shared BUSINESS journal, while an ADMIN also sees the SYSTEM journal.
The same day and filters are visible differently by role: a WORKER only sees the shared BUSINESS journal, while an ADMIN also sees the SYSTEM journal.
The fresh (unfrozen) day query re-run by the update button; it includes the late login event.

mutations.reason: The canonical journal must stay traced to Q-041.
A BUSINESS event always has an author.
LOGIN_SUCCEEDED is a SYSTEM event.
Only an uninitiated LOGIN_FAILED may omit the actor; LOGOUT needs an initiator.
An accepted batch must never be authored by a null actor.
An attempt/phase key must be unique.
A declared expected event id must resolve and match the computed page.
A non-empty query page must not be declared empty.
A query page must not declare an extra event.
The cursor page must declare its true next_cursor.
Dropping the frozen upper bound would let the new event shift the page.
A blocked author with accessible events must stay in the actor list.
Every listed actor alias must resolve.
A later accessible event means has_new_events=true.
A read operation must not change the journal size.
User audit responses must be no-store.
The return audit operation_id must link return_operation_id.
The LT-03.4b descriptor must have a canonical representative event.
The dictionary event must bind the actual timeline draft revision.
A published event must bind the publication comment.
The return lifecycle must expose the QUARANTINE_RETURNED success event.
occurred_at must be an RFC3339 UTC Instant.
The error code must be declared by the specific audit operation.
A WORKER query must never return a SYSTEM event.

update_button.reason: Finite update-button semantics: the frozen page reports the observed newest; a later event raises the indicator; pressing update re-runs the same filter without the old cursor and surfaces the new event; the indicator then clears.
